findings.title: Case-sensitive email lookup in BlockedEmail allows trivial bypass
findings.body: `BlockedEmail.should_block?(email)` queries `BlockedEmail.where(email: email).first` using an exact, case-sensitive match, and `BlockedEmail` does not normalize `email` (e.g., via `Email.downcase`) on save or lookup. Because `User` validates `email` before downcasing it (or if a user signs up with uppercase characters like `Spammer@example.com` while `spammer@example.com` is in `blocked_emails`), the blocked email check can be bypassed simply by changing the casing of the email address.

findings.title: Double validation during user creation increments BlockedEmail match_count twice
findings.body: In `UsersController#create`, when `SiteSetting.call_discourse_hub?` is enabled, `user.valid?` is called on line 168 and then `user.save` (which runs validations again) is called on line 172. Because `EmailValidator` calls `BlockedEmail.should_block?(value)`, which mutates and saves `match_count` as a side effect of validation, a single signup attempt with a `:do_nothing` (or `:block`) record will increment `match_count` multiple times if validations run more than once.

findings.title: Changing email does not validate against BlockedEmail or domain restrictions
findings.body: In `UsersController#change_email`, an `EmailToken` is created with `user.email_tokens.create(email: lower_email)` and an activation email is sent without running `EmailValidator` on the new address. When the user later confirms the token via `EmailToken.confirm`, if `EmailToken` updates the user's email or if `EmailToken` itself does not use `EmailValidator`, a user can either bypass `BlockedEmail` on email change or receive a confirmation email for an address that will fail validation upon confirmation.
